title: Mikrotik KNOT Gateway HL9 An outdoor Wi-Fi HaLow IoT gateway with GbE, WiFi 6, BLE 5.1, 4G LTE Cat 1 bis, and GNSS
summary: MikroTik KNOT Gateway HL9 is an IP66-rated outdoor IoT gateway that combines 915 MHz Wi-Fi HaLow (802.11ah), Bluetooth 5.1, Wi-Fi 6, LTE Cat 1 bis, Gigabit Ethernet, and GNSS. The gateway supports asset tracking, remote sensor monitoring, industrial IoT, and agricultural applications. Built around a dual-core Qualcomm IPQ-5010 ARM64 processor, it features 256MB RAM and 128MB NAND flash. title: Renesas RZ/T2N Cortex-A55/R52 industrial MPU supports four-axis motor control, TSN Ethernet, EtherCAT
summary: Renesas RZ/T2N industrial MPU supports up to four-axis motor control and includes PWM timers, encoder interfaces, and trigonometric accelerators. It s designed for industrial robots, programmable logic controllers (PLCs), motion controllers, and multi-axis servo drives. The MPU features up to two 1.2 GHz Arm Cortex-A55 cores for application processing and two 800 MHz Cortex-R52 cores for real-time control. It also integrates a three-port Gigabit Ethernet switch with TSN support and industrial Ethernet protocols such as EtherCAT, PROFINET RT/IRT, and EtherNet/IP. This feature set allows real-time motor control, industrial networking, and Linux applications to run on a single chip, reducing the need for separate processors. The MPU can also work as an industrial Ethernet network controller or device, depending on the application. title: LocalDot Open-source PCB for 3rd-gen Amazon Echo Dot enables Home Assistant support (Crowdfunding)
summary: AAElectronics LocalDot is an open-source replacement mainboard that converts a 3rd-generation Amazon Echo Dot into a local voice assistant compatible with Home Assistant. The board replaces one of the two original PCBs while reusing the existing microphones, speaker, buttons, LEDs, and enclosure, so the device works without relying on Amazon s cloud services. The board combines an ESP32-S3 for WiFi connectivity and device control with an ESP32-P4 for audio processing. It supports the original four-microphone array with beamforming, on-device wake-word detection, and local voice commands through Home Assistant. Installation requires no soldering or enclosure modifications, and the device still uses the original Echo Dot power adapter.
